analysis: Examined SSDBlockIndex.swift base/head and the docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md head excerpts (lines 284-562), plus metadata for SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator.swift, whose source body was not supplied in this batch. The only visible patch excerpt for it shows shared/exclusive per-path leases, FIFO grants, and a non-waiting tryUpgrade. The SSDBlockIndex change adds a read-only lastAccess(tag16:) accessor at head 137-140. It also threads an optional unusedSince through retireOwnedEntries/retireActiveEntries (head 231, 288, 295). The intent is that whole-root TTL expiry spares a loaded store's file that the in-memory index saw hit within the TTL, and persists that hit as the file's mtime. Relevant threat: T-041 (TTL is the reuse-window bound, max 1800s, with SEC-035 sign-off required to raise it). This does not extend the TTL beyond its sliding definition: lastAccess is set only by real hits and writes, and the docs (line 377) cap mtime lag at ttlSeconds/30. However, the implementations of retireOwnedEntries(unusedSince:) and SSDOwnedEntryRetirement were not visible, so I could not confirm the comparison direction. Integration should verify, in SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.swift and SSDWholeRootMaintainer.swift, that: (1) the comparison is lastAccess > now - ttlSeconds; (2) a future mtime or future lastAccess cannot pin a file indefinitely, since freshBytes at head 77 skips the age check when now < lastAccess (pre-existing behavior); (3) the mtime rewrite uses no-follow IO under the exclusive lease; (4) budget eviction cannot be starved by repeated lease-busy skips. Also check that the FIFO lease ordering in SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator prevents writer starvation and that tryUpgrade is refused when waiters exist. No concrete regression was identified in the visible lines. Docs changes are consistent with T-041 posture (encryption, HMAC names and TTL max are unchanged).
